assignment.objective: Find transversal mechanisms that eliminate several richer-mode dependencies at once using scheduled Chat alone and remain operational with zero optional monthly quota.

own_state_predecessor.handling: Observed only for role-local lineage. Its unrelated base-work semantics were not resumed because current Phase-1 no-restore policy is active.

candidate.name: content-addressed event segments plus a single CAS head
candidate.mechanism: Store each logical transition as an immutable content-addressed event with prev-event and idempotency op_id. Store only the current stream pointer/snapshot in one small mutable HEAD file. Every scheduled-Chat writer fetches the current HEAD blob, derives a new event, creates the immutable event, then advances HEAD using the fetched blob SHA as compare-and-swap. A stale writer is rejected and must reread/re-evaluate. The applied_op_ids set lets a retry recognize an already-applied logical operation and suppress a duplicate effect.
transversal_outcomes_targeted: crash/restart reconstruction by replay or snapshot plus tail
duplicate retry suppression via stable operation identifiers
stale-writer conflict rejection without an external coordinator
role-local handoff/continuation state without hosted execution
candidate.storage_compute_separation: Repository API is used only for lightweight transport/state. Interpretation, comparison and next-step reasoning happen in scheduled Chat; API volume is not used as compute.

public_sources.title: GitHub REST API endpoints for repository contents
public_sources.evidence: Create/update file contents uses the current blob sha for updates; the endpoint can return 409 Conflict. Concurrent contents mutations to the same path can conflict and should be serialized.

public_sources.title: GitHub REST API rate limits
public_sources.evidence: REST requests are rate-limited; 403/429 responses require waiting for retry-after/reset and repeated secondary-limit failures require increasing backoff. This candidate therefore treats GitHub as low-volume transport and checkpoints before retry.

public_sources.title: Azure Architecture Center: Event Sourcing pattern
public_sources.evidence: Append-only event streams support audit/replay and entity reconstruction; optimistic concurrency rejects an append if the stream changed and the handler must reload/re-evaluate/retry. Snapshots reduce long replay cost.

steps.action: created HEAD revision 1 and read it back
created immutable event 2 linked to event 1
advanced HEAD from revision 1 to revision 2 using the exact prior blob SHA

steps.observed: HTTP 409; path did not match stale blob sha
steps.postcondition: readback still showed revision 2, counter 2 and both intended op_ids

probe.inference_not_yet_crash_injected: If an immutable event is created but HEAD is not advanced, the event is unreachable from the authoritative HEAD and can be treated as an orphan. A retry can fetch HEAD, observe that op_id was not applied, and either reuse the deterministic event object or derive a replacement before a fresh CAS. This structural property is not yet an explicit crash/restart experiment.

assessment.tested_scope: single role-local event stream and one mutable HEAD pointer via GitHub Contents API
assessment.scoped_result: PASS for durable state + replay/audit structure + optimistic stale-writer rejection; duplicate-suppression precondition is present via applied_op_ids but duplicate retry was not separately mutation-tested
assessment.rate_limit_classification: GitHub REST has request-rate limits, so this route is acceptable only as low-volume transport with checkpoint/backoff and without API-volume-as-compute. Rate limiting can increase latency and remains an operational constraint.
assessment.root_acceptance: PARTIAL ONLY. This probe does not reproduce arbitrary shell/binary execution, browser/UI interaction, unavailable external effects or protected-primary operations. Those are unresolved Phase-1 children, not accepted handoffs.
assessment.conflict_check: All writes were confined to the authorized cross_field role-local namespace. No O, other-worker, downstream, shared-ledger or legacy semantic input was used.

limits_and_failure_modes: GitHub Contents API is rate-limited; 403/429 requires backoff and exact continuation rather than busy retry.
A single HEAD serializes one stream. Multi-entity atomic state requires a single root manifest/head or a higher-level transaction representation.
An event created before a failed HEAD CAS can become an orphan; authoritative replay must follow only HEAD-reachable events.
Repository content endpoints are not a bulk data/computation substrate; large logs should be segmented/sharded and snapshot periodically.
The tested mechanism cannot create capabilities that scheduled Chat does not expose. Missing effect classes remain unresolved children rather than being labeled irreducible handoffs.

frontier.reason: Tests whether one CAS root can safely coordinate several role-local objects and recover from an event-created/head-not-advanced crash equivalent without duplicate logical effects.
Specify exact checkpoint/backoff semantics for 403/429 so rate limits add latency but do not create a hosted-compute or manual-rescue dependency.

Map which richer-mode outcomes can be represented as Chat reasoning plus repository mutations and which absent effect classes remain unresolved, then seek transversal Chat-native substitutes rather than handoffs.

exact_next_action: Create two immutable logical-object event streams under one content-addressed root manifest referenced by a single CAS HEAD. Deliberately create a new event/root candidate without advancing HEAD to simulate interruption, then on a fresh read reconstruct solely from HEAD, verify the orphan is ignored, retry the same op_id and advance exactly once. Record all reads/writes and stale-CAS controls in the role-local namespace.
